headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: CrewAI’s broad workspace/tooling can ingest AutoGPT outputs and act on them without default isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and CrewAI reads the host working directory and accepts tool/model inputs, so a shared file bridge can carry attacker-controlled content into CrewAI. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented in either profile, so prompt-like content in AutoGPT outputs could be treated as instructions by CrewAI.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes untrusted instructions into a file that CrewAI later reads from the shared working directory
IF CrewAI parses AutoGPT-produced text as task instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Add a manual review step before CrewAI consumes AutoGPT output
Prefix handoff files with a strict schema and reject free-form text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and its working-directory file access plus broad network egress can expose sensitive material if AutoGPT places secrets or private data in shared files. AutoGPT also has filesystem access and shell execution, so the pair can move data from local files into external model/provider calls without a documented containment boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive data is present in the shared working directory or AutoGPT outputs
IF CrewAI forwards that content to model providers or tool integrations
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Mount separate per-agent directories
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict CrewAI tool integrations to non-sensitive endpoints
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inter-agent files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands and write to the filesystem, while CrewAI supports multiple instances with developer-defined shared state and no default self-isolation. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared resources, and AutoGPT’s lack of multiple-instance support does not prevent CrewAI from colliding with it.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or shared state
IF either agent writes files or shell-generated artifacts concurrently
mitigations: Run each agent in its own workspace
Serialize file writes with a lock file
Disable shared state between CrewAI instances
Avoid concurrent shell tasks on the same repo
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew and shared-memory design can treat upstream outputs as authoritative, and AutoGPT can generate arbitrary text, files, and shell-derived artifacts. Without a documented verification gate between them, AutoGPT errors can propagate into CrewAI actions, including tool calls or model-provider requests, making downstream mistakes likely and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF CrewAI consumes AutoGPT output as task context or shared memory
IF CrewAI agents act on that output without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Insert a human approval step between agents
Require structured outputs with validation
Compare AutoGPT claims against source files before action
Limit CrewAI to read-only analysis of AutoGPT output
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while AutoGPT can access the filesystem and shell, so compliance depends on how data is placed into the shared workspace. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, but the default lack of isolation and broad egress create a plausible retention/logging exposure path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF CrewAI forwards that data to external model providers or logs it
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use a local-only model backend
Review logging and retention settings
Separate environments by data class
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
